title: Discourses on Livy
author: Niccolò Machiavelli
translator: Ninian Hill Thomson, 1883 (public domain, Project Gutenberg #10827)
blurb: The other Machiavelli: a love letter to republics, arguing that free peoples are wiser and steadier than princes.

commonwealth.m: A state governed for the common good.
commonwealth.e: The town ran itself like a small commonwealth.

prudent.e: A prudent driver slows down in rain.

cards.title: Assume the worst
cards.text: Anyone founding a state must write laws as if people will misbehave when given the chance — not because everyone is evil, but because good laws must hold even when they are.
cards.quote: all men are bad, and will always, when they have free field, give loose to their evil inclinations
cards.qMean: Design rules assuming people will misuse freedom.
cards.qLife: Apps add two-step login because some people will try to break in.
cards.cap: Cesare Maccari, Appius Claudius in the Senate · public domain

cards.title: The people are wiser
cards.text: Surprising from the author of The Prince: a people, he argues, is more prudent, more stable and has better judgement than a prince.
cards.quote: a people is more prudent, more stable, and of better judgment than a prince.
cards.qMean: Ordinary people together judge better than a single ruler.
cards.qLife: A team vote often beats the boss's hunch.
cards.cap: Forum and Column of Trajan restored (Ancient Rome) engraving · public domain

cards.title: Plan for the next leader
cards.text: Good states don't depend on one great ruler; they arrange a steady succession of able ones.
cards.quote: in every well ordered commonwealth provision will be made for a succession of this sort.
cards.qMean: Well-run places plan who leads next.
cards.qLife: A family business training the next generation early.
cards.cap: Busts of Lucius and Marcus Junius Brutus · public domain
